title: Misleading .nvmrc file says '24' but project uses Bun, not Node/nvm
description: Verified: .nvmrc:1 — contains '24', implying Node.js v24 via nvm. The project uses Bun (packageManager: 'bun@1.3.14') and has no nvm-related configuration. This misleads developers into thinking Node/nvm is the runtime. `git status` shows .nvmrc as untracked (`?? .nvmrc`), meaning it was recently added but never committed.
spec:
1. Delete the `.nvmrc` file from the working tree.
2. Verify deletion with `cat .nvmrc` — should report file not found.
3. If Node.js version pinning is desired, document the Node version requirement in README.md and package.json engines field instead (engines.node already specifies '>=24.0.0 <25.0.0').

IMPORTANT: After resolving this finding, locate the feature.json file(s) in .aidd/features/ whose spec originally produced the code or pattern that caused this audit finding. Update those feature.json spec(s) to prevent this issue from being reintroduced during a feature-based rebuild.
